label: prop:trace-locality-meets-gs-non-locality
title: Reconciliation: Markov locality of single generators vs. Gröbner-Shirshov non-locality of composite braids
html:
Proposition. Reconciliation: Markov locality of single generators vs. Gröbner-Shirshov non-locality of composite braids

Let \beta = \sigma_{i_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_N} have Gröbner–Shirshov normal form \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\beta) = e_{j_1} \cdots e_{j_M}. Three facts reconcile the locality of single Hecke crossings with the non-locality of Gröbner–Shirshov reduction.

  1. Markov locality. For every x,
  \mathrm{tr}_{M, n+1}(x \sigma_n) = z\, \mathrm{tr}_{M, n}(x), \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_{M, n+1}(x \sigma_n^{-1}) = z_{-}\, \mathrm{tr}_{M, n}(x), \qquad
  z_{-} = z - (q - q^{-1}).

A single newly-added crossing contributes a scalar — depending only on the crossing sign — independent of the upstream history. 2. GS non-locality. \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\beta) depends on the full word; rewriting rules act non-locally across \beta. 3. Product factorisation. The Markov trace of the normal form decomposes locally, \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho_{\mathrm{NF}}(\beta)) = \prod_{i = 1}^{M} \widehat{V}_i(q), where each vertex volume \widehat{V}_i depends only on its own normal-form generator and modified coefficients produced by the GS algorithm.
